Consider the following program in C:

The output of the program is ________. (answer in integer)

Note: Assume that the program compiles and runs successfully.
explanation:
Step 1: Variable Scoping and Shadowing
In C, declaring a variable inside an inner block (e.g., inside the `if` block) shadows any variable with the same name declared in an outer scope (e.g., the function parameter `i`).

Step 2: Trace `func(9, 10)` Execution
• The `main()` function invokes `func(9, 10)`, initializing parameter $i = 9$ and parameter $j = 10$.
• The condition `if (i < j)` evaluates to `9 < 10` (true).
• Inside the `if` block, a new block-scoped variable `int i = 0;` is declared, shadowing parameter $i$.
• The `while (i < 10)` loop increments this local $i$ until it reaches 10.
• Upon exiting the `if` block, the local block-scoped $i$ goes out of scope.

Step 3: Determine Output
• The line `printf("%d", i);` is executed outside the `if` block, where $i$ refers to the function parameter $i$.
• Parameter $i$ remained untouched with a value of $9$.

Therefore, the output of the program is 9.
